alignments.note: Postpositive δέ rendered by the clause-initial But.

πρό rendered above in the priority sense. The ASV spreads Πρὸ πάντων over separate words that each answer to a token, so rule 94's single-word precondition for a compound prepositional unit is not met and rule 2 splits the pair.
Substantival πάντων expanded with the generic noun things; rule 17 keeps the head on all.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive my; the vocative is anarthrous so no article competes.
Anarthrous vocative; rule 89's article case does not arise.
Present imperative rendered by the bare verb.
Ordinary prohibitive μή rendered not; the following μήτε clauses carry their own English words, so rules 41 and 59 do not empty it.
μήτε rendered neither; the supplied by belongs to the article under rule 21.
Rule 21: the article takes the English the and the supplied case preposition by rides with it, headed on the.
Noun stands bare, its determiner and case preposition being on the article.
Second μήτε rendered nor.
As at s009, the article carries by the under rule 21.
Noun bare after its article takes the determiner.
Third μήτε rendered nor.
Indefinite τινά rendered any; the phrase is anarthrous, so any is the indefinite's own word and not a supplied determiner.
ἄλλον rendered other.

Anarthrous phrase with no article to anchor the supplied preposition, so rule 21's determinerless clause leaves by with the noun, discontinuously under rule 15 as `Ἐπ᾽ ἐσχάτου χρόνου` → the … time does at rule 58. Attaching by to μήτε at t017 is the competing reading; rule 21 places a case preposition with the token bearing the determiner, and here that is the noun.
Second δέ rendered but.

Third-person imperative ἤτω rendered let … be; the imperative auxiliary let is a rule 9 helper inside the verb's own unit, headed on the lexical be, discontinuous under rule 15. Rule 73's `κόπους … παρεχέτω` → let no man trouble me forbids splitting off a bare let headed on itself.

One genitive pronoun realized by two possessives, the ASV repeating *your* before each coordinated member; one discontinuous realization of the single token under rule 15. The corpus is unanimous for this reading — seven units, none conceding — wherever one genitive pronoun stands over coordinated nouns and the ASV repeats the possessive, and JHN.11.48 `ἡμῶν καὶ τὸν τόπον καὶ τὸ ἔθνος` → *both our place and our nation* and TIT.1.15 `αὐτῶν καὶ ὁ νοῦς καὶ ἡ συνείδησις` → *both their mind and their conscience* are this verse's shape token for token, the pronoun fronted outside both members. Rule 103's `added` reading is not taken and is not conceded: that rule is for supplied lexical content whose source token is spent, a pronoun is exactly what rule 7 names, and no corpus unit has ever stranded a repeated possessive off a pronoun that is present. JAS.5.3 was corrected to this same reading, which is rule 24.

Rule 20: the possessive *your*, licensed by the fronted ὑμῶν scoping over both coordinated members, occupies the determiner slot, so the article realizes nothing. TIT.1.15 and JHN.11.48 leave the articles of such a coordination empty in the same way.
First Ναί rendered yea.
Second ναί, the predicate, rendered yea.
Expressed καί rendered and.

As at s021: the second *your* is the single ὑμῶν's own under rule 20, so this article realizes nothing. Rule 76's availability test does not move it — ὑμῶν is spent only on possessives, not on an English word of some other syntactic role, and one word's English split across a coordination is still that word's. A reference comparison reports this token as represented, and that report is not a correction; BSB flags only this article and not s021, an asymmetry the ASV analysis has no reason to reproduce.
First Οὔ rendered nay.
Second οὔ, the predicate, rendered nay.
Rule 40: the subordinating ἵνα is realized by the word introducing its English clause, here that.
Inflected subjunctive taking its English subject; rule 9 heads the unit on the lexical verb fall.

Ordinary negative rendered not; no negative indefinite follows, so rules 41 and 59 do not arise. Rule 39's `ἵνα μή` → lest is scoped to a cluster rendered by one English word; here the ASV writes that … not, so each particle keeps its own word and the pair splits.
Expressed preposition rendered under; the variant decision keeps the base reading covering s030 and s031.
Anarthrous noun rendered judgment.

review_notes: Returned unchanged in structure: all 32 source and 37 target ids are still partitioned exactly once, every head is a member of its own array, and no unit's membership or status was altered. Only three notes were expanded (s001, s017, s018, s025, s029) to name the rules a later reader would otherwise have to rederive.

The three supplied by's are placed by rule 21: with the article where one stands (s009, s012) and with the noun where the phrase is anarthrous (s017), the latter discontinuous under rule 15 with any/other left as their own units, which rule 15 requires. Rule 36 is not in play, since no Greek preposition is expressed for these accusatives.

The two supplied your's both fold onto ὑμῶν. Checked against rule 76: its availability test empties an article's competitor only where the ASV has spent the pronoun on an English word of some other syntactic role (a subject we, an object us), and here ὑμῶν is spent on possessives alone, so rule 20 proper holds and both τό articles stay unrepresented. Giving t029 to s025 under rule 20's second arm, or marking it added under rule 103's main clause, are the competing readings; the unit notes name them.
The marginal reading cited in the verse note (let yours be the yea, yea) is not the ASV text and was not followed.
ἵνα μή is split rather than joined because rule 39's noncompositional cluster requires a single English word; that is now stated in the s029 note.

Heads reviewed independently of edges per rule 28: ἤτω heads on be rather than the auxiliary let (rules 17, 73), πέσητε on fall rather than the supplied ye (rule 9), and πάντων on all rather than the generic things (rule 17).
